name: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189)

selection_odds.basis: Points-tested EOI pool via SkillSelect; 65-point minimum to enter, but 2025-26 invitation rounds averaged 85-95+ points for competitive occupations, with some (e.g. accountants) receiving zero invitations

application_window.note: Quarterly invitation rounds (roughly August, November, February, May); 2025-26 program year quota of approximately 16,887 invitations was effectively exhausted after just two rounds (August and November 2025)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an occupation on the Medium and Long-Term Strategic Skills List (MLTSSL), plus a positive skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a positive skills assessment for an MLTSSL-listed occupation.

value.note: 65-point minimum on the points test (age, English, skilled employment, qualifications, etc.) to submit an Expression of Interest — realistic invitation threshold is commonly 85-95+ points for competitive occupations

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least 65 points on the points test to submit an Expression of Interest via SkillSelect — but 65 points rarely results in an actual invitation; competitive occupations commonly require 85-95+ points in practice.
requirements.fix_path: Improve points-test factors (age, English test score, skilled employment years, qualifications) before submitting or resubmitting an EOI.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being under 45 at the time of invitation.
This requires at least Competent English (broadly IELTS 6 or equivalent across all bands).
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved English test at the required level.

evidence_required.document: Positive skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority

outcome.duration_length: indefinite — permanent visa on grant, no further application needed to remain permanently
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: the visa itself is permanent, but the travel facility attached at grant typically expires after 5 years — see notes on Resident Return Visas

sources.title: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) Points-tested stream - Department of Home Affairs

notes: STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE from every European country in this dataset, worth flagging prominently: Australia's points-tested visas are PERMANENT ON GRANT — there is no separate 'temporary work visa → apply for PR after 5 years' pipeline the way UK/Germany/Netherlands/Portugal/Spain/France all work. pr_after_months is 0 because the grant itself IS the permanent status; citizenship_after_months (12) reflects only the mandatory minimum 12 months holding a permanent visa, on top of the broader 4-year total residence requirement (see au_citizenship_conferral) — the 12-month figure here is deliberately the SHORTER of the two constraints since total residence time was very likely accumulated on temporary visas before this grant. Classic Two-number trap flagged honestly: the OFFICIAL pass mark is 65 points, but this is genuinely close to meaningless in isolation — real invitation rounds in 2025-26 required 85-95+ points for most occupations, and some occupations (accountants) received ZERO invitations despite a nominally open program. Any secondary source presenting '65 points' as sufficient for a realistic assessment is technically accurate but practically misleading — this is a different kind of staleness/misleading-figure risk than seen in the European datasets (not a wrong number, but a technically-true number stripped of essential context). Visa Application Charge $4,640 AUD for the main applicant (reduced for partner/children), among the highest visa fees in this entire dataset.
